title: Establish cross-SDK retry/backoff defaults and idempotency semantics (Python/TS/Go)
creator: Daniel Kim
description:
Purpose: define a single, pragmatic set of cross-SDK defaults and clear semantics for retries, backoff with jitter, and idempotency keys across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. This ticket captures the proposed defaults, streaming ergonomics, edge cases, and implementation notes so all SDKs behave consistently by default while remaining configurable.

Why this matters: customers build production services on top of Redwood SDKs. Inconsistent retry behavior causes surprising duplicate side effects, cost spikes, and hard-to-debug reliability differences between languages. A simple, conservative, and documented default reduces customer surprises and makes support/observability signals comparable across platforms.

Proposed defaults (opinionated but conservative):
- Retry policy (by operation class):
  - Idempotent/semantically-safe ops (embeddings, reranking, non-streaming read-only endpoints): max_retries=3, initial_delay_ms=100, multiplier=2.0, max_delay_ms=5000, jitter=full-jitter (sleep = random(0, computed_delay)).
  - Best-effort non-idempotent ops (single-request text completion endpoints that modify server state or are used for billing-side effects): default max_retries=0. Retries disabled unless client supplies an idempotency key.
  - Streaming generation: treat streaming as non-retryable by default; retries allowed if a server-side resumable protocol exists or if the client provides a persistent idempotency_key AND server returns a request_id that can be used to resume.

- Retryable error taxonomy (cross-SDK canonical mapping):
  - HTTP/REST: retry on 429 (RateLimit), 502/503/504 (gateway/backend transient errors), and 408 (Request Timeout). Do NOT retry on 4xx client errors except 429.
  - gRPC: retry on UNAVAILABLE, RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, ABORTED (transient concurrency), and DEADLINE_EXCEEDED. Do NOT retry on PERMISSION_DENIED or INVALID_ARGUMENT.
  - Application-level transient errors: treat responses with body {"error":"temporarily_unavailable"} or error.code=="rate_limit_exceeded" as retryable (mapped by SDK parser).
  - Network-level errors: DNS failures, connection resets, TLS handshake failures: treat as retryable (up to max_retries).

- Idempotency keys and headers:
  - Standard header name: X-Redwood-Idempotency (SDKs should expose a typed param idempotency_key).
  - Semantics: if idempotency_key is provided, server guarantees at-least-once deduplication for the request key for a TTL of 24 hours (server-side). SDKs may safely retry idempotent or non-idempotent endpoints up to configured max_retries when key provided.
  - Generation guidance: when performing client-initiated side-effecting actions (billing events, dataset uploads, job creation), libraries should default to generating a UUIDv4 idempotency key unless the caller supplies one. Document tradeoffs in README.

- Streaming ergonomics tradeoffs and recommendations: 
  - Default: streaming endpoints are treated as non-retryable. This keeps semantics simple for end-users who expect streaming tokens to be consumed once.
  - Resumable streaming (future work): define an opt-in resumable-stream protocol where the server returns a resume_token/request_id in the initial connection handshake. SDKs will store that token and support an explicit resume() API. This is out-of-scope for initial rollout but included in acceptance criteria.
  - For server-side partial responses (e.g., partial outputs persisted), require explicit server contract before enabling automatic retries.

Cross-SDK implementation notes (per-language):
- Python: provide a RetryPolicy class in redwood_sdk.retries with method should_retry(error, attempt) and compute_backoff_ms(attempt). Integrate with httpx.AsyncClient and synchronous transport. Default transport-level retry middleware should be enabled for idempotent ops. Expose config via client(retry_policy=...).
- TypeScript: implement a RetryMiddleware for fetch/axios-based transports. Expose client options { retry: { enabled: boolean, maxRetries: number, backoff: { baseMs, multiplier, maxMs, jitter } } } and top-level idempotencyKey param. Avoid enabling retries for streaming Response.body reads by default.
- Go: add retry.go helper with RetryWithContext(ctx, op func() error, policy RetryPolicy). Use context-aware sleeps with time.After and math/rand for jitter. Ensure retries respect ctx.Deadline/Cancel.

Acceptance criteria:
- SDKs implement and ship defaults described above behind a single, documented config surface.
- Comprehensive unit tests that assert retry/no-retry decisions for: HTTP 429, 500, 400, gRPC UNAVAILABLE, network errors, and idempotency key provided.
- End-to-end smoke test that simulates transient 503 and confirms a 3-attempt retry on embeddings endpoint in Python/TS/Go.
- Documentation pages and code examples in SDK READMEs and CHANGELOG entries explaining default behavior and how to opt out or customize.

Open questions / decisions to resolve in follow-ups:
1) Max default initial_delay_ms: 100ms proposed; some internal low-latency customers prefer 50ms. Consider per-tier defaults (hosted vs dedicated) or expose client-side tuning presets ("conservative" vs "aggressive").
2) Exact TTL for server-side idempotency dedupe: 24h recommended, product to confirm.
3) Streaming resume protocol scope: separate RFC/Design spike required with product and backend.

2026-03-09 - Security Review (note): Punting explicit HSM/KMS handling to separate ticket; idempotency keys are not secrets but should not be logged in plaintext. SDKs to redact keys in debug logs by default.

2026-03-12 - Daniel Kim: Updated taxonomy after discussion with infra: treat gRPC ABORTED as retryable for short-form retries (<=2 attempts) due to optimistic concurrency conflicts. Marked in description.
